stance_basis: letter demanding restudy of noise impacts and commitment to abatement measures before project proceeds
summary: State Senator Kurt A. Frank submitted a formal letter raising three major concerns about the Airport Spur project: that it will exceed Federal Noise Standards, that children at Hamlin Garland Elementary School will be educationally harmed by noise, and that the Division of Highways is improperly excusing itself from compliance obligations. He requested a restudy of noise effects and a firm commitment to abatement measures including air conditioning and/or insulation for the school, indicating conditional support contingent on these remedies.
complaint_summary: Senator Frank's letter raises three concerns: the project will exceed Federal Noise Standards (pointing to discrepancies between stated compliance and Figure 13 data at Hamlin Garland School site 15 and site 24), that school children will be educationally harmed by noise, and that the Division of Highways is improperly excusing itself from taking all necessary steps to comply with noise standards, requesting a restudy and a commitment to abatement measures.

statement.text:
The following are comments regarding the General Mitchell Field for your consideration. I have three major concerns about the project: I am concerned that the project will exceed the Federal Noise Standards; I am concerned that the children at the Hamlin Garland Elementary School will be slighted their full educational opportunity if the project is constructed as proposed; I am not convinced that it is proper for the Division of Highways to excuse themselves from taking all necessary and reasonable steps to assure compliance with these standards on the grounds that they are not legally bound to the standards on this project.
To prove my first statement, I point to the discrepancy between your statements on compliance with the noise standards and the data that you present. On page 96 you state that the maximum noise levels that we are concerned about are 70 dBA for exterior noise and 55 dBA for interior noise. You state on pgs. 94, 95 that:
1) "Predicted 1990 noise levels at Hamlin Carland School during normal school hours will be within the acceptable limits of the noise standards.
yet in the data that you present in Figure 13, it demonstrates that in 1990 at site 15, the Hamlin Garland School, predicted L10 Noise Levels will exceed the established noise level of 70dBA. What worsens the problem is that the computer model that predicts noise levels, did not take into account local traffic noise or airplane noise.

Page Two Mr. Herried
2) "Traffic on the proposed Airport Spur will not contribute significantly to predicted noise levels for the year 1990."
At noise measurement site No. 24, the corner of Howell Ave. and the proposed interchange for the Spur, the field measurements in Figure 12 were taken for only one time period and found to exceed the limits. In Figure 13 the 1990 predicted L10 noise levels are not predicted for site 24 because "local traffic will be the predominant source of noise."
What must be clear is that at site 24 the proposed airport spur carrying a predicted 18,800 vehicles on an average day will contribute to the further deterioration of the noise standards. The statement leaves the impression that the Airport Spur will not contribute to noise level standards deterioration. I believe that the citizens of Wisconsin deserve a more thorough analysis of the effect of this project on the noise standards than has heretofore been presented before they lend their approval for construction. I find three objections to the present treatment of the noise standards:
1. There is an inadequate assessment of the effect of the Airport Spur on further deterioration of the noise standards, especially at site 24. As further evidence that the Spur will contribute to deterioration of the standards, I point to measurements taken and predicted at sites 11, 14, 15, 18, 19, and 23 all points that will be affected, noise-wise, by the Spur. The effects range from 2-15 dBA's depending on the spot. I must add that because of the position of site 24 the department should offer predictions of the noise level.
2. I have learned that the study was conducted at a time when the East-West runway to Mitchell Field was not in operation and at a time when a major airline, Northwest Airlines, was on strike and not operating planes at Mitchell Field. The absence of these two normal sources of noise will result in measured noise levels less than would normally exist:
3. The Division of Highways seems to be taking the attitude that in comparison with other noise sources, the Airport Spur contributes little, therefore it is undeserving of concern. I contend that the area in question is a sensitive one relative to the problems of noise pollution. In such a sensitive area, it seems reasonable to expect that potential projects are carefully screened to determine if they will exacerbate the noise pollution problem. Although the Airport Spur may contribute less

Tage Three Mr. Herried
to the problem than other sources its mere presence is going to worsen the noise levels. Therefore there must be an outstanding need before such a project is approved in an area like this.
I am concerned that the children at the Hamlin Garland Elementary school will be slighted of their full educational opportunity if the project is constructed as proposed. I have already alluded to the discrepancy between the stated compliance with the noise standards and the data which doesn't uphold the statement. This contradiction is of great concern in light of the statement on Page 95, "Air conditioning Hamlin Garland Elementary School is not warranted for the predicted noise levels inside and outside of the school building will marginally satisfy the acceptable noise standards" (emphasis added).
It does not appear that the noise standards will even marginally meet the standards. What we face in effect then is a collision between two goals that we hold in great esteem in Wisconsin, seeking the fullest educational opportunity for our children, and seeking safe and efficient transportation facilities.
I see two potential resolutions to this conflict. Abandon the existing plans for the project and propose an alternative route or agree to take all necessary steps to protect Hamlin Garland Elementary School from the distractions of noise, including air conditioning, insulation and or any other necessary steps. This latter resolution seems to me to be the only method of achieving the two goals the state has set forth.
This leads to my third concern. In Policy and Procedure Memorandum 90-2, Noise Standards and Procedures, the Federal Highway Administration states that (The noise standards)
"should be viewed as maximum levels, recognizing that in many cases, the achievement of lower noise levels would results in even greater benefits to the community."
Throughout the memorandum, the FHWA makes it clear that compliance with these standards is in the overall public interest. I am not convinced that it is proper for the Division of Highways to excuse themselves from taking all necessary and reasonable steps to assure compliance with the standards on the grounds that they are not legally bound to the standards. Yet I believe that this is the position that the Division has taken. I cannot agree that noise abatement measures are unwarranted until the noise levels are reached as stated on page 115. I believe that the additional costs in time and money to study and implement measures to reach the standards in the future when they are exceeded make it far more economical to take all necessary steps now rather than waiting till later.

Page Four Mr. Herried
Further I cannot agree that because a federal or state law apparently in the public interest does not demand compliance on this particular project that the Division of Highways should then not take the necessary steps to minimize the effects of this project on the noise standards. I shouldn't have to remind the leaders of the Division that their responsibility for protecting the public health and safety extends to preventing needless distractions for school children.
In conclusion I would request two things from the Division of Highways:
1. A restudy of the effects of the proposed project on the noise levels in the area;
2. A commitment to take whatever steps are necessary including air conditioning and/or insulation to Hamlin Garland Elementary School to reduce the potential noise distractions.
Sincerely yours,
KURT A. FRANK State Senator 7th District
